structured.answer: I'd go with Meitav's "עוקב מדדי מניות" track (7867): it went up the most of anything I saw, 25.86% over 3 years and 17.25% over 5, with a 0.65% fee, and Meitav is a name I know. Haven't done anything yet; first step is finding out how to open it at Meitav.

stuck.where: Return column, 'פחות מ־3 שנים' / 'פחות מ־5 שנים'

findings.what: 143 rows in one long list grouped by company; it's very hard to compare the same kind of track across companies on a phone
Every row repeats 'מניות', 'מט"ח', 'ההחסכון', 'ההפקדה' and clock icons, so you reread them on every row just to find what changes
findings.where: Fee and stocks/foreign-currency columns on every row

findings.what: Many tracks show 'פחות מ־3 שנים' or 'עוד לא דווח' instead of numbers, including several S&P 500 tracks
findings.where: Return and fee columns, e.g. אלטשולר שחם, מגדל, איילון

findings.what: Two fee lines per row ('ההחסכון' and 'ההפקדה') with no plain explanation of the difference
Ring charts are colour-only; 'מט"ח' is never explained beside them
Not clear whether returns are total or yearly; the 5-year figure being lower than the 3-year one confuses
The S&P 500 filter button is easy to miss among about 20 small buttons at the top
Fees only shown as percentages, never in shekels
